title: Pic of a proper curve: divisibility, n-torsion, cokernel
statement:
Let $C$ be a proper smooth connected curve of
genus $g$ over algebraically closed $k$, and let $n$ be prime
to $\operatorname{char}k$. Then

$$
\operatorname{Pic}(C)[n]\cong(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)^{2g},
\qquad
\operatorname{coker}\bigl(n:\operatorname{Pic}(C)\to
\operatorname{Pic}(C)\bigr)\cong\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z,
$$

and $\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)$ is $n$-divisible.

proof.text: Apply the torsion and degree-zero divisibility component theorems to f, n and the nonzero cast hypothesis.

For the cokernel conjunct, use the Picard decomposition Pic(C) ≃ ℤ × P0 and degree-zero divisibility. Map the integer coordinate into ZMod n; integer cast gives surjectivity. An nth power maps to zero. Conversely a class in the kernel has integer coordinate n*z and its P0 coordinate has an nth root; the inverse decomposition gives an nth root of the class. The first isomorphism theorem identifies the quotient with Multiplicative (ZMod n). Introduce the three conjunctions. This is the local hc proof, not a call to the retired standalone cokernel declaration.
